topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's scope and intended learning outcomes before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Mutation-driven evolution and epigenetic transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine cellular changes that drive tumor development, extending the account of mutation-based clonal selection to transformation through altered gene regulation.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy and its capacity for self-renewal influence tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties on mutation-bearing cells and enable tumor development.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells as a vulnerability that therapy can target.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling and computational approaches reveal tumor evolution and interactions within the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains malignancy through the convergence of cellular fitness and a permissive environment, including how that framework bears on susceptibility at different stages of life.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces therapy as the next lecture's subject.
